justification: Assessment returned INVALID and identified the same defect as ground truth: step 0009's sub-claim ('otherwise n+i <= prod p^{nu_p(k)} = lcm(1,...,k) <= n') gives no contradiction in the case i=0, n=lcm(1,...,k), so the non-strict hypothesis n >= lcm(1,...,k) makes the theorem false at the boundary. It supplied the identical primary witness k=3, n=6 ([6,9] = {6,7,8,9}; only 7 has a prime factor > 3, count 1 < k+1-pi(k) = 2; 6 = 2*3 has no prime-power divisor exceeding 3) and the identical second witness k=2, n=2. Both witnesses check out arithmetically, and the proposed repair (strict n > lcm(1,...,k)) matches the ground-truth diagnosis.
